summary: Mozambique's official eVisa portal sorts visitors into four groups: 17 nationalities, mostly from southern and eastern Africa, are visa-exempt for 30 or 90 days; 29 others, including the US, the UK, Canada, Japan and much of Western Europe, need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) for stays of up to 30 days; citizens of Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Nepal and Somalia must apply at an embassy; and everyone else applies online for an eVisa before travel.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Mozambique?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Mozambique's official eVisa portal (evisa.gov.mz) lists 17 nationalities, mostly from southern and eastern Africa, as visa-exempt for 30 or 90 days. Citizens of 29 countries, including the US, the UK, Canada, Portugal and most of Western Europe, need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) before travel, for stays of up to 30 days. Citizens of Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Nepal and Somalia cannot use the portal and must apply at a Mozambican embassy. Everyone else applies online for an eVisa before travelling.

faq.question: Is there a fee for the eTA?
faq.answer: Decree 10/2023, which exempted citizens of about 30 countries from the visa, sets a MZN 650 processing fee, payable when pre-registering at evisa.gov.mz at least 48 hours before boarding; the portal now lists these countries under the eTA scheme. Mozambique's High Commission in London describes the fee as paid on arrival. The UK Foreign Office says British travellers also pay a USD 37 visa fee (about USD 47 in total), online. The portal itself does not publish the eTA fee, so check the amount when you apply.

faq.question: Can I get a Mozambique visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Only in limited cases. The migration service's visa rules provide a border visa, valid for two entries and 30 days and not extendable, for nationals of countries where Mozambique has no embassy or consulate, or on reciprocity. The official eVisa portal does not offer a visa on arrival: it sorts nationalities into visa-exempt, eTA, eVisa and embassy-only, and tells travellers to carry the printed approval for boarding and arrival. Apply before you travel.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Mozambique?
faq.answer: Yes — tourist stays can normally be extended once, for up to 30 further days, at migration service (migração) offices in provincial capitals, though the border visa issued on arrival cannot be extended. Apply before your current permission expires; overstays are fined per day.

faq.question: Is Mozambique safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Check current advisories before you go. Australia's Smartraveller advises a high degree of caution in Mozambique overall and says do not travel to Cabo Delgado province and parts of Nampula and Niassa provinces, nor on stretches of the EN1 and EN6 roads. The UK government says you must carry your passport at all times.
